What the endpoint is for, in a sentence or two.
shell.studio.field.endpoint.entity.help: The entity whose records the endpoint reads or changes.
shell.studio.field.endpoint.process.help: The process that the endpoint runs when it is called.

shell.studio.field.endpoint.input.name: Name
shell.studio.field.endpoint.input.name.h: The name the caller uses for this value.
shell.studio.field.endpoint.input.type.h: What the value holds, such as text, a number, a date or a reference.
shell.studio.field.endpoint.input.requir: Whether a caller must send this value.
shell.studio.field.endpoint.input.maxLen: The most characters a text value may hold.

shell.studio.field.endpoint.input.values: The values the input accepts, when it has a fixed list.

shell.studio.field.form.name: Name
shell.studio.field.form.name.help: The name that identifies the form in the file and in Studio.
shell.studio.field.form.description.help: What the form is for, in a sentence or two.
shell.studio.field.form.entity.help: The entity whose records the form edits.
shell.studio.field.form.sections.help: The parts of the form, each with a title and the fields that it shows.
shell.studio.field.form.sections.name: Name
shell.studio.field.form.sections.name.he: The name that identifies the section in the file.
shell.studio.field.form.sections.title: Title
shell.studio.field.form.sections.title.h: The heading people see above the section.
shell.studio.field.form.sections.visible: An expression that decides whether the section shows, or always when none is set.
The fields the section shows, in order.
The field the form shows, by its name.
Whether people can see the field but not change it.
An expression that decides whether the field shows, or always when none is set.
An expression that makes the field required while it is true.
An expression that makes the field read only while it is true.
How wide the field is, in columns of the form's grid.
shell.studio.field.process.name: Name
shell.studio.field.process.name.help: The name that identifies the process in the file and in Studio.
shell.studio.field.process.description.h: What the process is for, in a sentence or two.
shell.studio.field.process.startConditio: A condition that must hold before the process can start.
The expression that must be true before the process starts.
The message people see when the condition does not hold.
shell.studio.field.process.entity.help: The entity whose records the process runs on.
shell.studio.field.process.parameters.he: The values that a caller passes in when it starts a process that has no entity.
shell.studio.field.process.parameters.na: The name that expressions use to read the parameter.
shell.studio.field.process.parameters.ty: The type of value the parameter holds.
shell.studio.field.process.start.help: The step that the process begins with.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.name: Step name
shell.studio.field.process.steps.name.he: The name that identifies the step, which other steps point to.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.type.he: What the step does, such as a task for a person, a decision or a timer. Changing it removes the properties that the new type does not allow.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.next.he: The step that runs after this one.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.otherwi: The step that runs when no branch matches.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.branche: Each branch has a condition and the step that runs when the condition is true.
The expression that decides whether the process takes this branch.
The step that runs when the process takes this branch.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.label: Label
shell.studio.field.process.steps.label.h: The text, picked from the application's texts, that names the task for the person who does it.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.assigne: Who does the task: the user that an expression gives, or the people who have a role.
An expression that gives the user who does the task.
The role whose people can do the task.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.form.he: The form that the person fills in to complete the task.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.dueIn.h: How long the task may stay open, as an ISO 8601 duration such as P3D. Leave it empty for no due time.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.deadlin: An optional time limit. When it runs out, the process moves to another step.
How long after the task opens the deadline falls, as an ISO 8601 duration such as P5D.
The step that the process moves to when the deadline falls.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.escalat: What happens when a task stays open too long: it is given to someone else, people are notified, or both.
How long after the task opens the escalation happens, as an ISO 8601 duration such as PT4H.
Turn on to give the task to someone else when the escalation happens.
An expression that gives the user who gets the task.
The role whose people get the task.
Turn on to send a message when the escalation happens.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.timer.h: Whether the step waits for a length of time or until a point in time.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.wait.he: How long the step waits, as an ISO 8601 duration such as PT1H.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.until.h: An expression that gives the time that the step waits until.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.event.h: The event that the step waits for. Only the events about the process's entity are listed.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.when.he: An optional expression over the event's fields. Only an event that makes it true lets the process go on.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.timeout: An optional limit on the wait, and the step that the process moves to when the limit runs out.
How long the step waits for the event, as an ISO 8601 duration such as P2D.
The step that the process moves to when the wait runs out.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.process: The child process that this step starts.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.subject: Subject record
An expression that gives the record that the child process runs on.
shell.studio.field.process.steps.outcome: The ways that the person can finish the task, each with the step that runs after it.
The name that identifies the outcome.
The text, picked from the application's texts, that names the outcome for the person who does the task.
The step that runs when the person chooses this outcome.
shell.studio.field.connector.name: Name
shell.studio.field.connector.name.help: The name that identifies the connector in the file and in Studio.
shell.studio.field.connector.description: What the connector is for, in a sentence or two.
shell.studio.field.connector.baseUrl.hel: The URL binding that holds the address of the service. Only the binding's name is stored, and its value is set in the tenant's settings.
shell.studio.field.connector.timeout.hel: How long one call may take, as an ISO 8601 duration such as PT30S, up to PT2M. Thirty seconds when none is set.
shell.studio.field.connector.idempotency: The name of the request header that carries the idempotency key. Leave it empty when the service has no such header.
shell.studio.field.connector.auth.type.h: How the connector signs in to the service: not at all, with a bearer token, with a header or with OAuth2.
The secret binding that holds the bearer token sent with each call. Only the binding's name is stored, and its value is set in the tenant's settings.
shell.studio.field.connector.auth.name: Header name
shell.studio.field.connector.auth.name.h: The name of the header that carries the secret.
The secret binding that holds the value of the header. Only the binding's name is stored, and its value is set in the tenant's settings.
shell.studio.field.connector.auth.tokenU: The URL binding that holds the address where the connector gets its access token. Only the binding's name is stored, and its value is set in the tenant's settings.
shell.studio.field.connector.auth.client: The secret binding that holds the ID the connector signs in with. Only the binding's name is stored, and its value is set in the tenant's settings.
The secret binding that holds the secret the connector signs in with. Only the binding's name is stored, and its value is set in the tenant's settings.
The scope to ask for with the access token, 1 to 2000 characters. Leave it empty to ask for none.
shell.studio.field.connector.auth.audien: The audience to ask for with the access token, 1 to 2000 characters. Leave it empty to ask for none.
The name that processes use to call the operation.
The method of the request. A GET sends no body.
The path after the base URL. A name in curly braces takes the value of the input with that name, and idempotencyKey takes the operation's identity.
Another operation of this connector that finds an earlier call by its idempotency key. It must be a GET.
The values the operation sends, each with a name and a type.
The name of the value to send.
The type of the value. An object or a list holds nested fields.
Where the value goes in the request: the body, the path, the query or a header. The body is the default.
Whether the caller must give the value.
The fields inside an object or a list.
The name of the nested value.
The type of the nested value. An object or a list holds more nested fields.
Whether the caller must give the nested value.
The values the operation returns, read from the JSON response.
The name of the value. It is read from the response property of that name, unless a source is set.
Whether the response must hold the value.
A JSON Pointer into the response body that says where the value is read, such as /shipment/tracking/number. Leave it empty to read the property named like the output.
